note: Two separate measurements. A = API speed on the server (private network, no internet). B = what a user's browser waits for one HTTPS request over the internet (health check only).

A_server_private_api.setup: DigitalOcean droplet, Singapore, 1 vCPU / 2 GB (Ubuntu 24.04); production stack running (docker-compose.prod.yml: uvicorn 1 process + Postgres 16 + UI + Caddy); benchmark ran in a throw-away container from the api image on the compose network, calling http://api:8000 (private API, not through Caddy); one client, sequential calls
A_server_private_api.photo: synthetic 4032x3024 JPEG, no plate (detector runs, char CNN skipped)

B_mac_https_health.client: Ari's Mac (macOS-26.5.2-arm64-arm-64bit), Python urllib, one client, sequential calls
B_mac_https_health.setup: public internet -> Caddy (HTTPS, Let's Encrypt) -> api /health (runs SELECT 1 on Postgres); urllib opens a NEW TCP + TLS connection per request (no keep-alive) = worst case per call

network_ping_ms.note: ICMP ping Mac -> server, same session
